follow-up time: The study period was from May 2020 to August 2021, encompassing the first and second waves of the pandemic.
exposure: First wave of COVID-19 pandemic (May 2020 - February 2021)
Second wave of COVID-19 pandemic (March 2021 - August 2021)
cohort: 249 pregnant women who tested positive for COVID-19 admitted to Tata Main Hospital, Jamshedpur, India from May 2020 to August 2021
finding: The study found a significantly higher number of moderate to severe COVID-19 cases and maternal deaths during the second wave compared to the first wave, along with a higher incidence of severe oligohydramnios and cesarean sections.
mod_finding: The study found a higher incidence of cesarean section in COVID-19 positive pregnant women during the second wave compared to the first wave.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was reported in both waves, but specific data not provided.
